title: Get started with pubflow
text: pipeflow parameter plain R value, default step function’s argument. pubflow parameter (param) value attributes describe : label, limits, description, . param config collects params analysis: kind param checks values: choice_param() allows one choices (value factor), numeric_param() number min max. source = "user" marks params user sets, app report can pick .
code: library(pubflow)  config <- param_config(     xVar = choice_param(         "Temp.Celsius",         choices = c("Temp.Celsius", "Wind", "Solar.R"),         label = "Predictor",         source = "user",         description = "Variable that explains the ozone concentration"     ),     level = numeric_param(         0.95,         label = "Confidence level",         min = 0.5,         max = 0.999,         source = "user"     ),     title = param(         "Ozone in New York",         label = "Report title",         source = "user"     ) ) config # <param_config: 3 params> #  name  type      value                     label            #  xVar  factor    <factor[1]: Temp.Celsius> Predictor        #  level numeric   0.95                      Confidence level #  title character Ozone in New York         Report title

title: Get started with pubflow
text: next steps turn results outputs document can show: pub_table() makes table column labels number decimal places, pub_figure() figure caption, pub_text() text Markdown. table figure made functions defined outside pipeline (coef_table() fit_figure()). matters figures: ggplot keeps environment made , plot made inside pipeline’s code keep pipeline alive every copy figure.
code: library(ggplot2)  coef_table <- function(model, level) {     ci <- confint(model, level = level)     coefs <- data.frame(         term = rownames(ci),         estimate = coef(model),         lower = ci[, 1L],         upper = ci[, 2L]     )     pub_table(         coefs,         caption = sprintf("Coefficients with %g%% confidence limits", 100 * level),         labels = c(             term = "Term",             estimate = "Estimate",             lower = "Lower",             upper = "Upper"         ),         digits = c(estimate = 3L, lower = 3L, upper = 3L)     ) }  fit_figure <- function(model, data, xVar) {     coefs <- coef(model)     p <- ggplot(data, aes(.data[[xVar]], .data$Ozone)) +         geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +         geom_abline(intercept = coefs[[1L]], slope = coefs[[2L]])     pub_figure(p, caption = "Linear model fit", width = 6, height = 3.5) } pip |>     pip_add("coef_table", function(model = ~fit, level = 0.95) {         coef_table(model, level)     }) |>     pip_add("plot", function(model = ~fit, data = ~prep, xVar = "Temp.Celsius") {         fit_figure(model, data, as.character(xVar))     }) |>     pip_add("summary", function(model = ~fit) {         r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared         pub_text(sprintf(             "The model explains **%.0f%%** of the variance of the ozone concentration.",             100 * r2         ))     })

code: library(shiny)  ui <- fluidPage(     fluidRow(         column(4, pub_params_ui("params")),         column(8, pub_viewer_ui("viewer", height = "90vh"))     ) )  server <- function(input, output, session) {     pip <- pip_clone(pip) # every session gets its own pipeline     params <- pub_pipeline_params_server("params", pip)     doc <- reactive({         params$revision() # run again after every change of a param         pip_run(pip, lgr = NULL)         pip[["report", "out"]]     })     pub_viewer_server("viewer", doc) }  shinyApp(ui, server) shiny::runApp(system.file("examples", "report-app", package = "pubflow"))

code: # A param is its value plus information about it p <- param("abc", label = "Name", source = "user") p #> param<character>: abc #>   label: Name #>   source: user #>   validity: <function> param_value(p) #> [1] "abc"  # Numbers within bounds; params can be used like their values alpha <- numeric_param(0.05, label = "Significance level", min = 0, max = 1) alpha < 0.1 #> [1] TRUE param_validity(alpha, value = 1.5) #> [1] "value must be less than or equal to max (1)"  # A number as text keeps its trailing zero limit <- numeral_param("80.0", label = "Ozone limit (ppb)") param_value(limit) #> [1] "80.0"  # One of several choices trans <- choice_param("log", choices = c("none", "log", "sqrt"),                       label = "Transformation") levels(trans) #> [1] "none" "log"  "sqrt" trans == "log" #> [1] TRUE param_validity(trans, value = "exp") #> [1] "value must be one of: none, log, sqrt"  # Own constructors: wrap one of the above and fix some of its arguments yes_no_param <- function(x = c("yes", "no"), label = "Yes/No", ...) {     choice_param(match.arg(x), choices = c("yes", "no"), label = label, ...) } show <- yes_no_param("no", label = "Show points?") as.character(show) #> [1] "no"  bound_param <- function(..., side = c("lower", "upper")) {     numeral_param(..., side = match.arg(side)) }  # Own validity: a positive whole number. Wrap numeric_param() and pass your own # rule; it replaces the default one, so it has to check everything it needs. pos_integer_param <- function(     x,     label = "positive integer",     description = label,     max = .Machine$integer.max,     validity = \(x) {         if (length(x) == 0) return("value cannot be empty")         if (anyNA(x)) return("value cannot be NA")         if (any(x != round(x))) return("value must be a whole number")         if (any(x < 1)) return("value must be positive")         if (any(x > max)) return(paste("value must not exceed", max))         ""     },     ... ) {     numeric_param(         x, label = label, description = description, min = 1, max = max,         validity = validity, ...     ) } n <- pos_integer_param(3L, label = "Sample size") param_validity(n, value = 2.5) #> [1] "value must be a whole number" param_validity(n, value = 0) #> [1] "value must be positive" param_validity(n) #> [1] ""  # Params shown and checked together limits <- param_group(     list(         lower = bound_param("1.0", label = "Lower", side = "lower"),         upper = bound_param("2.0", label = "Upper", side = "upper")     ),     label = "Limits" ) |>     add_validity(\(x) {         if (as.numeric(x$lower) < as.numeric(x$upper)) "" else             "lower must be below upper"     }) param_validity(limits, value = list(lower = "3", upper = "2")) #>                       group                       lower  #> "lower must be below upper"                          ""  #>                       upper  #>                          ""
